column3: “Loved of a companion” is rendered “loved by her husband,” and “commits adultery” “an adulteress”; “cakes of grapes” is rendered “raisin cakes.”
NASB supplies “shekels of”; “a homer of barley and a lethech of barley” is rendered “a homer and a half of barley.”
“And also I to you” is rendered “so I will also be toward you.”
“Be in dread” is rendered “come trembling”; “at the end of the days” is rendered “in the last days.”
